architecture.goal: Extend the validated phase-1 runtime with explicit operational orchestration, retry control, duplicate protection, and pending-record lifecycle transitions while preserving per-provider FIFO isolation.
runtime_shape: EventBridge Scheduler triggers Producer Lambda once per day
Producer Lambda resolves target date and reads PENDING records for that date
Producer Lambda publishes one SQS FIFO message per eligible record
SQS FIFO preserves same-provider ordering through MessageGroupId
Orchestrator Lambda consumes SQS messages and starts one Step Functions execution per work item
Step Functions acquires duplicate protection, updates pending-record state, invokes the business consumer, retries transient failures, captures terminal failures, and closes operational state
Consumer Lambda performs the provider API call and persists business outcomes in the results table
DynamoDB stores pending records, final results, and dedicated idempotency state
explicit_non_goals_for_phase: Redesign of pending-table partitioning for 1M+ scale

module_boundaries.responsibility: Start the daily orchestration flow and support target-date override.
Read PENDING work for a target date and dispatch provider-aware FIFO messages.
Preserve strict ordering inside a provider and allow concurrency across providers.
Bridge SQS messages into Step Functions executions and enrich input with operational metadata such as TTLs.
Control retries, duplicate blocking, lifecycle transitions, and failure closure.
Execute one provider request and classify outcomes into success, transient error, or terminal error.
Store final success and failure evidence for audit.
Prevent duplicate independent execution of the same logical work item.

interfaces_and_contracts.name: ProviderRecord
interfaces_and_contracts.purpose: Represent one logical work item flowing from pending storage through orchestration and execution.

interfaces_and_contracts.name: SqsMessage
interfaces_and_contracts.purpose: Carry one ProviderRecord into the provider-isolated execution transport.

interfaces_and_contracts.name: ProviderApiResult
interfaces_and_contracts.purpose: Represent a successful business outcome returned by the provider adapter.

interfaces_and_contracts.name: IdempotencyRecord
interfaces_and_contracts.purpose: Represent operational duplicate-protection state for one logical work item.

interfaces_and_contracts.name: Workflow metadata
interfaces_and_contracts.purpose: Provide orchestration-only operational values to the state machine input.

data_and_storage_design.decision: Keep the date-based pending-table access pattern from phase 1, but phase 2 starts mutating record lifecycle state.
data_and_storage_design.usage: Producer reads only PENDING records for the target date; the orchestration flow updates records to IN_PROGRESS, COMPLETED, or FAILED.
data_and_storage_design.note: This is a temporary operational baseline; large-scale repartitioning remains a phase-3 concern.

data_and_storage_design.decision: Continue using a durable results table as the final business history of successes and failures.
data_and_storage_design.usage: Consumer persists successful results and terminal failures; the orchestration layer may also persist an exhausted transient failure as a final failed outcome.
data_and_storage_design.note: Results are not reused as the primary duplicate-protection mechanism.

data_and_storage_design.decision: Introduce a dedicated DynamoDB table keyed by logical work-item identity.
data_and_storage_design.usage: The orchestration flow acquires an IN_PROGRESS lock before execution and closes it as COMPLETED or FAILED.
data_and_storage_design.note: TTL is short because the table is operational rather than historical.

dependency_and_library_decisions.decision: Use AWS Step Functions Standard Workflow for retry orchestration and operational state progression.
dependency_and_library_decisions.rationale: Phase 2 needs explicit Retry and Catch behavior, deterministic closure paths, and a visible operational story beyond raw queue retries.

dependency_and_library_decisions.decision: Keep SQS FIFO as the provider-isolation transport layer.
dependency_and_library_decisions.rationale: SQS FIFO already enforces same-provider ordering and remains the correct boundary for serialization.

dependency_and_library_decisions.decision: Keep the Lambda business consumer as a separate unit invoked by Step Functions.
dependency_and_library_decisions.rationale: This preserves separation between business execution and orchestration concerns while minimizing domain rewrites.

dependency_and_library_decisions.decision: Use a dedicated DynamoDB table for idempotency instead of embedding duplicate control in pending or results tables.
dependency_and_library_decisions.rationale: It keeps responsibilities separate, supports conditional writes cleanly, and aligns with robust operational design.

behavioral_decisions.decision: The orchestrator Lambda enriches state-machine input with TTL metadata.
behavioral_decisions.rationale: The workflow needs numeric TTL values for operational tables without depending on dynamic timestamp arithmetic inside Step Functions.

behavioral_decisions.decision: Duplicate work items are closed early when the idempotency lock or pending-state transition cannot be acquired.
behavioral_decisions.rationale: This prevents a second independent execution while keeping the runtime deterministic.

behavioral_decisions.decision: Transient retries are handled by Step Functions, not by direct SQS retry semantics alone.
behavioral_decisions.rationale: This centralizes retry policy, catch behavior, and final failure closure in one operational model.

behavioral_decisions.decision: Exhausted transient failures are persisted as final failed business outcomes.
behavioral_decisions.rationale: A work item that consumed its retry budget still needs an auditable final result.

behavioral_decisions.decision: Pending records move to COMPLETED on success and FAILED on terminal or exhausted closure.
behavioral_decisions.rationale: The pending-table lifecycle must reflect system-level processing status, not just raw provider status.

changes: Reintroduce an SQS-driven orchestrator Lambda between queue transport and business execution.
Invoke the consumer Lambda from Step Functions instead of directly from SQS.
Remove phase-1-only SQS consumer handler from the active runtime path.
Keep business error classification through TransientApiError and TerminalApiError.
Add explicit shared types for idempotency and completed lifecycle state.
Preserve the producer contract from phase 1 while extending downstream operational control.
Provision Step Functions, orchestrator Lambda, and idempotency table in CDK.
Grant StartExecution to the orchestrator Lambda.
Grant Step Functions rights to mutate pending records, persist exhausted transient failures, and update idempotency state.
Update pending records through PENDING -> IN_PROGRESS -> COMPLETED/FAILED.
Store duplicate-protection state independently from final business outcomes.

failure_modes_and_edge_handling.case: No pending records exist for the target date
A record is no longer PENDING when selected or transitioned
failure_modes_and_edge_handling.handling: The orchestration path treats it as already claimed or no longer eligible and prevents independent duplicate execution.
The duplicate work item path ends early without producing a second business execution.
The consumer persists a success outcome, the workflow marks idempotency COMPLETED, and the pending record becomes COMPLETED.
The consumer persists terminal failure, Step Functions catches the error, marks idempotency FAILED, and sets the pending record to FAILED.

failure_modes_and_edge_handling.case: The provider call fails transiently and retries are exhausted
failure_modes_and_edge_handling.handling: Step Functions persists an exhausted transient failure outcome, marks idempotency FAILED, and sets the pending record to FAILED.

failure_modes_and_edge_handling.case: The provider call fails unexpectedly with a non-domain exception
failure_modes_and_edge_handling.handling: The consumer wraps it as TransientApiError when possible; otherwise the workflow closes through a generic failure branch.

failure_modes_and_edge_handling.case: The orchestrator receives invalid SQS payload
failure_modes_and_edge_handling.handling: It reports the message as batch failure so queue semantics can manage redelivery or DLQ routing.

quality_gates: Producer tests from phase 1 continue passing.
Consumer tests continue proving success and terminal-failure business behavior.
Orchestrator tests prove one Step Functions execution per valid SQS message and failure reporting for invalid or failed starts.
CDK synth succeeds and reflects orchestrator + Step Functions + idempotency wiring.
Operational validation plan covers success, terminal failure, exhausted transient failure, and duplicate blocking.
expected_test_scenarios: Producer still dispatches one FIFO message per eligible PENDING record.
Orchestrator starts one state-machine execution per queue message.
Step Functions retries transient failures before closure.
Step Functions captures terminal failures without retry.
Duplicate lock acquisition failure prevents second independent processing.
Pending records transition to IN_PROGRESS, COMPLETED, and FAILED in the expected branches.
Results table contains one final outcome for each completed, terminal, exhausted, or duplicate-handled scenario as appropriate.

phased_implementation_plan.goal: Add resilience, idempotency, and operational state control to the validated phase-1 runtime.
tasks: Restore a business-consumer Lambda entrypoint for Step Functions invocation.
Introduce the orchestrator Lambda and Step Functions state machine.
Add a dedicated idempotency table and duplicate-protection logic.
Add pending-record state transitions for operational lifecycle visibility.
Persist exhausted transient failures as final business outcomes.
Remove phase-1-only runtime leftovers and validate the new flow in code and AWS.
definition_of_done: Orchestration is explicit and centered in Step Functions.
Retryable and terminal failures follow distinct operational paths.
Duplicate work items do not produce a second independent business execution.
Pending records reflect operational state progression.
The runtime, tests, and CDK stack all describe the same phase-2 architecture.

assumptions: The canonical idempotency key for phase 2 is recordId plus scheduledDate.
The business consumer remains responsible for success and terminal-failure persistence of direct provider outcomes.
Short-lived operational TTL values can be injected into workflow input by the orchestrator Lambda.
The queue DLQ remains infrastructure safety net, but the primary retry story for phase 2 lives in Step Functions.
